questions.q: What is the article mainly about?
options: Mortgage rates staying above 7 percent while housing sales sink
The Federal Reserve's decision to cut rates ahead of the 2026 election
The long history of 30-year mortgage lending and Freddie Mac's role
Mortgage rates dipping below 6 percent as the housing market rebounds
questions.explain: Rates remain above 7 percent and home sales are at multi-year lows.

questions.q: How did mortgage rates move recently?
options: They rose sharply after briefly falling to ultralow levels last year
They remained about the same as they had been the previous month
They slid for the fourth straight week but stayed above 7 percent
They dropped below 6 percent and then sparked a quick rebound
questions.explain: The passage says rates slid for a fourth week but remained above 7 percent.

questions.q: How did existing-home sales change in October from a year earlier?
options: They rose by around 9 percent from a year earlier
They fell by around 9 percent from a year earlier
They fell by about 1 percent from a year earlier
They were roughly unchanged from the year before
questions.explain: The report said existing-home sales fell 8.8 percent from a year earlier.

questions.q: What started pushing mortgage rates up again after they fell below 6 percent in February?
options: A Fed rate hike announced in March
The failure of a regional bank in March
A jump in unemployment claims in March
The attacks on Iran launched Feb. 28
questions.explain: Rates began rising after the US and Israel attacked Iran on Feb. 28.

questions.q: Why are homeowners unwilling to sell, according to the article?
options: Many locked in ultralow rates and don't want to give them up
Home prices are falling, so they expect to sell for less later
They fear job losses and want to keep their savings as a cushion
Buyers are unavailable because they cannot qualify for any loans
